verses.1:1: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
verses.1:2: And the Lord delivered into his hand Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and a portion of the vessels of the house of God; and he carried them away to the land of Shinar, into the house of his god, and he brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
verses.1:3: And the king told Ashpenaz, the overseer of the eunuchs, to bring in from the sons of Israel, and from the royal offspring and that of the rulers,
verses.1:4: youths in whom there was no blemish, handsome in form and educated in all wisdom, discerning in knowledge and trained in learning, and who were able to stand in the king's palace, so that he might teach them the literature and language of the Chaldeans.
verses.1:5: And the king appointed for them an allowance for each day from his own food, and from the wine from which he himself drank, so that, having been nourished for three years, afterward they might stand in the presence of the king.
verses.1:6: So there were among them, from the sons of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
verses.1:7: And the overseer of the eunuchs gave them names: to Daniel, Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
verses.1:8: But Daniel resolved in his heart that he would not be defiled from the king's table, nor from the wine of his drinking; and he asked the overseer of the eunuchs that he might not be contaminated.
verses.1:9: Now God gave Daniel favor and mercy in the sight of the chief of the eunuchs.
verses.1:10: And the chief of the eunuchs said to Daniel, "I fear my lord the king, who appointed food and drink for you; if he sees your faces thinner than the other young men of your own age, you will condemn my head to the king."
verses.1:11: And Daniel said to Malasar, whom the chief of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
verses.1:12: "Test us, I beg you, your servants, for ten days, and let legumes be given to us to eat, and water to drink;
verses.1:13: and examine our faces and the faces of the youths who eat the royal food; and just as you see, you will deal with your servants."
verses.1:14: Having heard a word of this kind, he tested them for ten days.
verses.1:15: Now after ten days, their faces appeared better and plumper than all the youths who were eating the royal food.
verses.1:16: So Malasar kept taking away the rations and the wine of their drinking, and giving them legumes.
verses.1:17: Now to these youths God gave knowledge and learning in every book and wisdom; and to Daniel, understanding of all visions and dreams.
verses.1:18: Therefore, when the days were completed after which the king had said that they should be brought in, the overseer of the eunuchs brought them into the presence of Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.1:19: And when the king had spoken to them, none were found among them all like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; and they stood in the presence of the king.
verses.1:20: And in every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found in them tenfold above all the diviners and magicians who were in his entire kingdom.
verses.1:21: Now Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus.
verses.2:1: In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar saw a dream, and his spirit was terrified, and his dream fled from him.
verses.2:2: Then the king commanded that the soothsayers, the magicians, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans be summoned to disclose his dreams to the king. When they had come, they stood before the king.
verses.2:3: And the king said to them, "I saw a dream, and confused in mind I do not know what I saw."
verses.2:4: And the Chaldeans answered the king in Syriac, "O king, live forever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will disclose its interpretation."
verses.2:5: And answering, the king said to the Chaldeans, "The matter has slipped from me; unless you disclose to me the dream and its interpretation, you will perish and your houses will be confiscated.
verses.2:6: But if you recount the dream and its interpretation, you will receive rewards, gifts, and great honor from me. Therefore disclose to me the dream and its interpretation."
verses.2:7: They answered a second time and said, "Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will disclose its interpretation."
verses.2:8: The king answered and said, "I know for certain that you are buying time, knowing that the matter has slipped from me.
verses.2:9: Therefore, if you do not disclose the dream to me, there is one sentence concerning you: that you have also fabricated a deceptive interpretation full of fraud to speak to me until the time passes. So tell me the dream, that I may know that you also speak its true interpretation."
verses.2:10: Then answering before the king, the Chaldeans said, "There is no man on earth who can fulfill your demand, O king; moreover, no king, however great and mighty, asks a matter of this kind from any soothsayer, magician, or Chaldean.
verses.2:11: For the matter that you seek, O king, is hard, and no one will be found who can disclose it in the king's sight, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with men."
verses.2:12: When he heard this, the king, in fury and great anger, commanded that all the wise men of Babylon should perish.
verses.2:13: And when the decree went out, the wise men were being put to death, and Daniel and his companions were sought out so that they might perish.
verses.2:14: Then Daniel inquired concerning the law and the decree from Arioch, commander of the king's military force, who had gone out to put to death the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:15: And he questioned him, who had received authority from the king, for what reason so cruel a decree had gone out from the presence of the king. So when Arioch had explained the matter to Daniel,
verses.2:16: Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time to disclose the solution to the king.
verses.2:17: And he went into his house and explained the matter to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions,
verses.2:18: so that they might seek mercy from the presence of the God of heaven concerning this secret, and that Daniel and his companions might not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:19: Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel through a vision in the night; and Daniel blessed the God of heaven,
verses.2:20: and speaking, he said, "May the name of the Lord be blessed from age even to age, because wisdom and strength are His.
verses.2:21: And He Himself changes times and ages; He removes kingdoms and establishes them; He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who understand instruction.
verses.2:22: He Himself reveals deep and hidden things, and knows what is set in darkness, and the light is with Him.
verses.2:23: To You, God of our fathers, I give thanks and praise You, because You have given me wisdom and strength, and now You have shown me what we asked of You, for You have opened to us the king's matter."
verses.2:24: After this Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and spoke to him thus: "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon; bring me into the king's presence, and I will recount the solution to the king."
verses.2:25: Then Arioch hurried and brought Daniel in to the king, and said to him, "I have found a man from the sons of the exile of Judah who will declare the solution to the king."
verses.2:26: The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Do you truly think you are able to disclose to me the dream that I saw and its interpretation?"
verses.2:27: And answering before the king, Daniel said, "The mystery about which the king asks, wise men, magicians, soothsayers, and diviners cannot disclose to the king;
verses.2:28: but there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, who has disclosed to you, King Nebuchadnezzar, what is to come in the last times. Your dream and the visions of your head on your bed are of this sort:
verses.2:29: You, O king, began to think on your bed about what would happen after this; and the One who reveals mysteries has shown you what is to come.
verses.2:30: To me also this secret has been revealed, not because of wisdom that is in me more than in all the living, but so that the interpretation might be made clear to the king, and that you might know the thoughts of your mind.
verses.2:31: You, O king, were watching, and look, there was as it were one huge statue; that statue, great and towering in height, stood opposite you, and its appearance was terrifying.
verses.2:32: The head of this statue was of finest gold, its chest and arms of silver, and its belly and thighs of bronze,
verses.2:33: while its legs were of iron; part of its feet was of iron, and part was of baked clay.
verses.2:34: You kept watching in this way until a stone was cut from a mountain without hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay, and shattered them.
verses.2:35: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed together and reduced as if to the fine dust of a summer threshing floor, which was carried away by the wind, and no place was found for them; but the stone that had struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
verses.2:36: This is the dream; we will also tell its interpretation before you, O king.
verses.2:37: You are a king of kings, and the God of heaven has given you kingdom, strength, dominion, and glory;
verses.2:38: and all places in which the sons of men dwell, and the wild beasts of the field, and also the birds of heaven, He has given into your hand, and He has set all things under your authority; you therefore are the golden head.
verses.2:39: And after you another kingdom will arise, inferior to you, of silver; and another, a third kingdom, of bronze, which will rule over the whole earth.
verses.2:40: And the fourth kingdom will be like iron: just as iron shatters and subdues all things, so it will shatter and crush all these.
verses.2:41: Moreover, because you saw part of the feet and toes to be potter's clay and part iron, the kingdom will be divided; yet it will arise from the rootstock of iron, just as you saw iron mixed with clay made of mud.
verses.2:42: And as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly baked clay, the kingdom will be partly solid and partly brittle.
verses.2:43: And whereas you saw iron mixed with clay made of mud, they will indeed mingle with human seed, yet they will not cling to one another, just as iron cannot be mixed with clay.
verses.2:44: Now in the days of those kingdoms the God of heaven will raise up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and its kingdom will not be handed over to another people; instead, it will shatter and consume all these kingdoms, and it itself will stand forever.
verses.2:45: Just as you saw that a stone was cut from the mountain without hands and shattered the clay, the iron, the bronze, the silver, and the gold, the great God has shown the king what is to come afterward; and the dream is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy."
verses.2:46: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and paid homage to Daniel, and commanded that they offer sacrifices and incense to him.
verses.2:47: Then speaking, the king said to Daniel, "Truly your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and the One who reveals mysteries, since you were able to open this secret."
verses.2:48: Then the king raised Daniel to high rank and gave him many great gifts; and he appointed him ruler over all the provinces of Babylon, and prefect of the magistrates over all the wise men of Babylon.
verses.2:49: And Daniel requested of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon; but Daniel himself remained at the doors of the king.
verses.3:1: King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue, sixty cubits in height and six cubits in width, and set it up on the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.
verses.3:2: Therefore King Nebuchadnezzar sent to assemble the satraps, magistrates, and judges, the commanders, rulers, and prefects, and all the princes of the regions, so that they might come together for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had erected.
verses.3:3: Then the satraps, magistrates, and judges, the commanders, rulers, and nobles who had been appointed to offices of authority, and all the princes of the regions were assembled, so that they might come together for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had erected. And they were standing before the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set in place.
verses.3:4: And a herald cried out loudly, "To you it is declared, peoples, tribes, and languages:
verses.3:5: at the hour in which you hear the sound of the trumpet, the pipe, the lyre, the harp, the psaltery, and the ensemble, and of every kind of music, fall down and worship the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
verses.3:6: But if anyone does not fall prostrate and worship, in that very hour he will be thrown into the furnace of burning fire."
verses.3:7: Therefore, after these things, as soon as all the peoples heard the sound of the trumpet, the pipe, the lyre, the harp, the psaltery, and the ensemble, and of all kinds of music, all the peoples, tribes, and languages fell down and worshiped the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
verses.3:8: And immediately at that very time, Chaldean men came forward and accused the Jews.
verses.3:9: And they said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "King, live forever!
verses.3:10: You, king, laid down a decree that every person who hears the sound of the trumpet, the pipe, the lyre, the harp, the psaltery, and the ensemble, and of every kind of music, should prostrate himself and worship the golden statue;
verses.3:11: and if anyone does not fall down and worship, he is to be thrown into the furnace of burning fire.
verses.3:12: Now there are Jewish men whom you appointed over the affairs of the region of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men, king, have despised your decree; they do not revere your gods, and they do not worship the golden statue that you have erected."
verses.3:13: Then Nebuchadnezzar, in fury and in anger, commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought in; and immediately they were brought before the king.
verses.3:14: And King Nebuchadnezzar, speaking out, said to them, "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not revere my gods and do not worship the golden statue that I have set up?
verses.3:15: Now therefore, if you are ready, at whatever hour you hear the sound of the trumpet, the pipe, the lyre, the harp, the psaltery, and the ensemble, and of all kinds of music, prostrate yourselves and worship the statue that I have made. But if you do not worship, in that very hour you will be thrown into the furnace of burning fire; and who is the god who will rescue you from my hand?"
verses.3:16: Answering, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "It is not necessary for us to answer you concerning this matter.
verses.3:17: For look, our God, whom we revere, is able to rescue us from the furnace of burning fire and to deliver us from your hands, king.
verses.3:18: But if He is unwilling, let it be known to you, king, that we do not revere your gods, and we do not worship the golden statue that you have erected."
verses.3:19: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the look of his face was altered toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego; and he commanded that the furnace be heated seven times more than it was accustomed to be heated.
verses.3:20: And he ordered the strongest men from his army to bind the feet of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the furnace of burning fire.
verses.3:21: And immediately those men, bound, with their trousers, turbans, shoes, and garments, were thrown into the middle of the furnace of burning fire.
verses.3:22: For the king's order was urgent, and the furnace had been heated excessively; furthermore, the flame of the fire killed those men who had thrown in Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
verses.3:23: But these three men, that is, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell into the middle of the furnace of burning fire, bound fast.
verses.3:24: And they were walking in the middle of the flame, praising God and blessing the Lord.
verses.3:25: And Azariah, standing, prayed in this way, and opening his mouth in the middle of the fire, he said:
verses.3:26: "Blessed are You, Lord God of our fathers, and praiseworthy and glorious is Your name forever,
verses.3:27: for You are just in all that You have done to us, and all Your works are true, and Your ways are right, and all Your judgments are true.
verses.3:28: For You have executed true judgments according to all that You have brought upon us and upon the holy city of our fathers, Jerusalem; for in truth and in judgment You have brought all these things because of our sins.
verses.3:29: For we have sinned, and have acted wickedly in departing from You, and have transgressed in all things;
verses.3:30: and we have not listened to Your commandments, nor observed them, nor done as You had commanded us so that it might go well with us.
verses.3:31: Therefore, all that You have brought upon us, and everything that You have done to us, You have done in true judgment;
verses.3:32: and You have handed us over into the hands of our enemies, who are wicked, utterly evil, and transgressors, and to an unjust king, the most evil beyond all the earth.
verses.3:33: And now we cannot open our mouth; we have become a shame and a reproach to Your servants and to those who revere You.
verses.3:34: Do not, we plead, hand us over forever for the sake of Your name, and do not annul Your covenant,
verses.3:35: and do not take away Your mercy from us, for the sake of Abraham Your beloved, and Isaac Your servant, and Israel Your holy one,
verses.3:36: to whom You spoke, promising that You would multiply their offspring like the stars of heaven and like the sand that is on the shore of the sea;
verses.3:37: for, Lord, we have been diminished more than all the nations, and we are lowly throughout the whole earth today because of our sins.
verses.3:38: And at this time there is no prince, or leader, or prophet, nor burnt offering, nor sacrifice, nor oblation, nor incense, nor place of firstfruits before You,
verses.3:39: so that we might find Your mercy; yet with a contrite soul and a spirit of humility may we be accepted.
verses.3:40: As with a burnt offering of rams and bulls, and as with thousands of fat lambs, so let our sacrifice be in Your sight today, that it may please You, for there is no shame for those who trust in You.
verses.3:41: And now we follow You with our whole heart; and we fear You, and we seek Your face.
verses.3:42: Do not put us to shame, but deal with us according to Your gentleness and according to the multitude of Your mercy.
verses.3:43: And rescue us by Your wonders, and give glory to Your name, Lord;
verses.3:44: and let all who show evils to Your servants be put to shame; let them be put to shame by all Your power, and let their strength be crushed;
verses.3:45: and let them know that You alone are the Lord God, and glorious over the whole world."
verses.3:46: And the king's attendants who had thrown them in did not stop heating the furnace with naphtha, tow, pitch, and brushwood,
verses.3:47: and the flame poured out forty-nine cubits above the furnace,
verses.3:48: and it burst out and burned those of the Chaldeans whom it found near the furnace.
verses.3:49: But the angel of the Lord descended with Azariah and his companions into the furnace, and drove the flame of the fire out of the furnace,
verses.3:50: and made the middle of the furnace like a blowing wind of dew, and the fire did not touch them at all, nor distress them, nor bring any trouble upon them.
verses.3:51: Then these three, as from one mouth, were praising, and glorifying, and blessing God in the furnace, saying:
verses.3:52: "Blessed are You, Lord God of our fathers, and praiseworthy, and glorious, and supremely exalted forever. And blessed is the holy name of Your glory, and praiseworthy and supremely exalted throughout all ages.
verses.3:53: Blessed are You in the holy temple of Your glory, and supremely praiseworthy and supremely glorious forever.
verses.3:54: Blessed are You on the throne of Your kingdom, and supremely praiseworthy and supremely exalted forever.
verses.3:55: Blessed are You, who look upon the depths and sit above the cherubim, and praiseworthy and supremely exalted forever.
verses.3:56: Blessed are You in the expanse of heaven, and praiseworthy and glorious forever.
verses.3:57: Bless the Lord, all works of the Lord; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:58: Bless the Lord, angels of the Lord; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:59: Bless the Lord, heavens; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:60: Bless the Lord, all waters that are above the heavens; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:61: Bless the Lord, all powers of the Lord; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:62: Bless the Lord, sun and moon; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:63: Bless the Lord, stars of heaven; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:64: Bless the Lord, all rain and dew; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:65: Bless the Lord, all spirits of God; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:66: Bless the Lord, fire and heat; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:67: Bless the Lord, cold and heat; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:68: Bless the Lord, dews and hoarfrost; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:69: Bless the Lord, frost and cold; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:70: Bless the Lord, ice and snows; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:71: Bless the Lord, nights and days; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:72: Bless the Lord, light and darkness; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:73: Bless the Lord, lightning and clouds; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:74: Let the earth bless the Lord; let it praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:75: Bless the Lord, mountains and hills; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:76: Bless the Lord, all things sprouting on the earth; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:77: Bless the Lord, springs; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:78: Bless the Lord, seas and rivers; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:79: Bless the Lord, whales and all things that move in the waters; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:80: Bless the Lord, all birds of heaven; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:81: Bless the Lord, all beasts and livestock; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:82: Bless the Lord, sons of men; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:83: Let Israel bless the Lord; let it praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:84: Bless the Lord, priests of the Lord; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:85: Bless the Lord, servants of the Lord; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:86: Bless the Lord, spirits and souls of the just; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:87: Bless the Lord, holy and humble of heart; praise and supremely exalt Him forever.
verses.3:88: Bless the Lord, Hananiah, Azariah, Mishael; praise and supremely exalt Him forever, for He has rescued us from the underworld and saved us from the hand of death, and delivered us from the middle of the burning flame, and rescued us from the middle of the fire.
verses.3:89: Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy is forever.
verses.3:90: Bless the Lord, God of gods, all devout ones; praise and give thanks to Him, for His mercy is for all ages."
verses.3:91: Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished, and rose up hastily, and said to his nobles, "Did we not throw three men shackled into the middle of the fire?" And answering the king, they said, "Truly, king."
verses.3:92: He answered and said, "Look, I see four men unbound and walking in the middle of the fire, and there is no harm in them, and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of God."
verses.3:93: Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the door of the furnace of burning fire and said, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come here." And immediately Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out from the middle of the fire.
verses.3:94: And having assembled, the satraps, magistrates, judges, and powerful men of the king observed those men, how the fire had held no power over their bodies, and the hair of their head had not been singed, and their trousers had not been altered, and the smell of fire had not passed through them.
verses.3:95: And Nebuchadnezzar broke out and said, "Blessed be their God, namely, the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent His angel and rescued His servants who believed in Him; and they altered the king's word and handed over their bodies so that they would not serve and would not worship any god except their own God.
verses.3:96: Therefore this decree has been laid down by me: that every people, tribe, and language, whichever speaks blasphemy against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, is to perish, and its house is to be laid waste; for there is no other god who is able to save in this way."
verses.3:97: Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
verses.4:4: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at peace in my house and thriving in my palace.
verses.4:5: I saw a dream that terrified me, and my thoughts on my bed and the visions of my head disturbed me.
verses.4:10: The vision of my head on my couch: I was watching, and look, a tree in the middle of the earth, and its height was immense.
verses.4:11: The tree was great and strong, and its tallness touched heaven; the sight of it reached all the way to the ends of the entire earth.
verses.4:12: Its leaves were most beautiful and its fruit exceedingly abundant, and in it was food for all. Beneath it lived animals and beasts, and in its branches the birds of heaven made their dwelling, and from it all flesh fed.
verses.4:13: I was watching in the vision of my head on my bed, and look, a watcher and a holy one descended from heaven.
verses.4:14: He cried out loudly and spoke in this way: "Cut down the tree and lop off its branches; shake off its leaves and scatter its fruits. Let the beasts that are beneath it flee, and the birds from its branches.
verses.4:15: Nevertheless, leave the shoot of its roots in the earth, and let it be bound with a band of iron and bronze among the grasses that are outside; and let him be moistened with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the wild beasts in the grass of the earth.
verses.4:16: Let his heart be changed from a human one, and let the heart of a wild beast be given to him, and let seven times change over him.
verses.4:17: It is decreed by the sentence of the watchers, and it is the word of the holy ones and the petition, until the living come to know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and He will give it to whomever He wills, and He will appoint the lowliest man over it."
verses.4:18: This dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. You, therefore, Belteshazzar, tell the interpretation quickly, because all the wise men of my kingdom are unable to declare the explanation to me; but you are able, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.
verses.4:19: Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, began to think silently within himself for about one hour, and his thoughts were disturbing him. And the king answered and said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream and its interpretation disturb you." Belteshazzar answered and said, "My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies.
verses.4:20: The tree that you saw, lofty and sturdy, whose height reaches to heaven, and the sight of it across all the earth,
verses.4:21: and its branches most beautiful and its fruit exceedingly abundant, and food for all in it, the beasts of the field living beneath it and the birds of heaven dwelling in its branches:
verses.4:22: it is you, king, who have been made great and have grown strong; and your greatness has increased and reached all the way to heaven, and your dominion to the ends of the entire earth.
verses.4:23: And as for the king seeing a watcher and a holy one descend from heaven and say, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it; yet leave the shoot of its roots in the earth, and let it be bound with iron and bronze among the grasses outside, and let him be sprinkled with the dew of heaven, and let his pasture be with the wild beasts, until seven times change over him':
verses.4:24: this is the interpretation of the sentence of the Most High, which has come upon my lord the king:
verses.4:25: They will cast you out from among men, and your dwelling will be with beasts and wild animals, and you will eat grass like an ox, and you will be drenched with the dew of heaven. Seven times will also change over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men and gives it to whomever He wills.
verses.4:26: And as for his commanding that the shoot of its roots, that is, of the tree, should be left: your kingdom will remain yours after you have come to know that dominion is heavenly.
verses.4:27: For this reason, king, let my counsel be pleasing to you, and redeem your sins with almsgiving, and your iniquities with acts of mercy toward the poor; perhaps He will forgive your offenses."
verses.4:28: All of these things came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.4:29: After the end of twelve months, he was walking about in the palace of Babylon.
verses.4:30: And the king answered and said, "Is this not great Babylon, which I myself built as a house of the kingdom, in the strength of my might and in the glory of my splendor?"
verses.4:31: And while the word was still in the mouth of the king, a voice rushed down from heaven: "To you it is spoken, King Nebuchadnezzar: Your kingdom will pass away from you,
verses.4:32: and they will cast you out from among men, and your dwelling will be with beasts and wild animals; you will eat grass like an ox, and seven times will change over you, until you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men and gives it to whomever He wills."
verses.4:33: In that same hour the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar, and he was cast out from among men, and he ate grass like an ox, and his body was soaked with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew in the likeness of eagles and his nails like those of birds.
verses.4:34: Therefore, after the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my reason was restored to me; and I blessed the Most High, and praised and glorified Him who lives forever, because His dominion is an everlasting dominion and His kingdom is from generation to generation.
verses.4:36: At that very time my reason returned to me, and I attained the honor and splendor of my kingdom; and my form returned to me, and my nobles and my magistrates sought me out, and I was restored in my kingdom, and greater magnificence was added to me.
verses.4:37: King Nebuchadnezzar, to all peoples, nations, and languages who live in the entire earth: may peace be multiplied to you. The Most High God has worked signs and wonders with me. Therefore it has pleased me to proclaim His signs, because they are great, and His wonders, because they are mighty; and His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and His dominion is from generation to generation. Now therefore, I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and magnify and glorify the King of heaven, because all His works are true and His ways are judgments, and He is able to humble those who walk in pride.
verses.5:1: King Belshazzar made a great banquet for his thousand nobles, and each one was drinking according to his age.
verses.5:2: Therefore, being already drunk, he commanded that the gold and silver vessels be brought which Nebuchadnezzar his father had carried away from the temple that was in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, and his wives and concubines, might drink from them.
verses.5:3: Then the gold and silver vessels were brought which he had carried away from the temple that had been in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines drank from them.
verses.5:4: They were drinking wine and praising their gods of gold and silver, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
verses.5:5: In that same hour fingers appeared, as of a man's hand writing opposite the lampstand on the surface of the wall of the royal palace; and the king watched the joints of the hand that was writing.
verses.5:6: Then the king's face changed, and his thoughts were disturbing him; and the joints of his loins were loosened, and his knees were knocking against one another.
verses.5:7: Therefore the king cried out loudly that they should bring in the magicians, the Chaldeans, and the diviners. And speaking out, the king said to the wise men of Babylon, "Whoever reads this writing and makes its interpretation clear to me will be clothed in purple, and will have a gold chain on his neck, and will be third in my kingdom."
verses.5:8: Then all the wise men of the king came in, and they could neither read the writing nor declare the interpretation to the king.
verses.5:9: Because of this, King Belshazzar was greatly disturbed, and his expression was altered; and his nobles also were troubled.
verses.5:10: Now the queen, on account of the matter that had happened to the king and his nobles, entered the banquet hall; and speaking out, she said, "King, live forever! Do not let your thoughts disturb you, nor let your face be altered.
verses.5:11: There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him, and in the days of your father knowledge and wisdom were found in him; for King Nebuchadnezzar your father also appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners, your father, I say, king,
verses.5:12: because a greater spirit, and prudence and understanding, and the interpretation of dreams, and the revealing of secrets, and the untying of bound things were found in him, that is, in Daniel, to whom the king gave the name Belteshazzar. Now therefore let Daniel be called, and he will tell the interpretation."
verses.5:13: Therefore Daniel was brought in before the king, and the king spoke first to him and said, "Are you Daniel, from the sons of the captivity of Judah, whom my father the king brought from Judea?
verses.5:16: Furthermore, I have heard about you that you are able to interpret obscure things and untie bound things. If therefore you are able to read the writing and declare its interpretation to me, you will be clothed in purple, and you will have a gold chain around your neck, and you will be the third ruler in my kingdom."
verses.5:17: In answer to these things, Daniel said before the king, "Let your gifts be for yourself, and give the presents of your house to another; yet I will read the writing to you, king, and I will show its interpretation to you. And this is the writing that has been set down: Mene, Tekel, Peres.
verses.5:23: but you have lifted yourself up against the Sovereign of heaven, and the vessels of His house were brought before you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines drank wine from them. You also praised gods of silver and gold, and of bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which neither see nor hear nor perceive; yet God, who holds your breath in His hand, and all your ways, you have not glorified.
verses.5:26: And this is the interpretation of the word. Mene: God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.
verses.5:27: Tekel: you have been weighed on the scales and have been found lacking.
verses.5:28: Peres: your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and Persians."
verses.5:29: Then, at the king's command, Daniel was clothed in purple, and a gold chain was placed around his neck; and it was proclaimed concerning him that he held authority as third in his kingdom.
verses.5:30: That same night Belshazzar, the Chaldean king, was killed.
verses.6:1: And Darius the Mede succeeded to the kingdom, being sixty-two years old.
verses.6:2: It pleased Darius, and he appointed one hundred and twenty satraps over the kingdom to be throughout his whole kingdom;
verses.6:3: and over them three princes, of whom Daniel was one, so that the satraps might render an account to them and the king might not suffer trouble.
verses.6:4: Therefore Daniel surpassed all the princes and satraps, because the Spirit of God was more abundant in him.
verses.6:5: Moreover, the king was planning to appoint him over the entire kingdom; so the princes and satraps were seeking a pretext that they might find against Daniel from the side of the king, and they could discover no grounds or suspicion, because he was faithful, and no fault or suspicion was found in him.
verses.6:6: Therefore those men said, "We will not find any pretext against this Daniel, unless perhaps in the law of his God."
verses.6:7: Then the princes and satraps approached the king stealthily and spoke to him in this way: "King Darius, live forever!
verses.6:8: All the princes of your kingdom, the magistrates and satraps, the senators and judges, have taken counsel that an imperial decree and an edict should go out: that everyone who asks any request from any god or man for thirty days, except from you, king, should be thrown into the den of lions.
verses.6:9: Now therefore, king, confirm the ruling and write the decree, so that what has been established by the Medes and Persians may not be altered, nor may anyone be permitted to transgress it."
verses.6:10: Accordingly, King Darius set forth the edict and established it.
verses.6:11: When Daniel learned this, that is, that the law had been established, he entered his house; and with the windows open in his upper room toward Jerusalem, three times a day he bent his knees, and worshiped, and gave thanks before his God, just as he had been accustomed to do before.
verses.6:12: Therefore those men, investigating very closely, found Daniel praying and imploring his God.
verses.6:13: And approaching, they spoke to the king concerning the edict: "King, did you not establish that every man who would ask anyone of the gods or men for thirty days, except you, king, should be thrown into the den of lions?" Answering them, the king said, "The word is true according to the decree of the Medes and Persians, which it is not permitted to transgress."
verses.6:14: Then answering, they said before the king, "Daniel, from the sons of the captivity of Judah, has paid no regard to your law and to the edict that you established, but three times a day he prays with his supplication."
verses.6:15: When the king heard this word, he was greatly grieved, and he set his heart on Daniel's behalf to deliver him, and until the setting of the sun he was laboring to rescue him.
verses.6:17: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions. And the king said to Daniel, "Your God, whom you always worship, He Himself will deliver you."
verses.6:18: And one stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, which the king sealed with his ring and with the ring of his nobles, so that nothing might be done against Daniel.
verses.6:19: And the king went away to his house and went to sleep without supper, and no food was brought before him; moreover, sleep also departed from him.
verses.6:20: Then the king, rising at first light, went in haste to the den of lions.
verses.6:21: And approaching the den, he called out to Daniel with a tearful voice and addressed him: "Daniel, servant of the living God, your God, whom you always serve, do you think He has been able to deliver you from the lions?"
verses.6:22: And Daniel, answering the king, said, "King, live forever!
verses.6:23: My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not harm me, because before Him righteousness was found in me; and before you as well, king, I have committed no offense."
verses.6:24: Then the king rejoiced exceedingly over him and commanded Daniel to be brought out of the den. And Daniel was brought out of the den, and no injury was found on him, because he believed in his God.
verses.6:25: And at the king's command, those men who had accused Daniel were brought and thrown into the den of lions, they themselves, and their children, and their wives; and they did not reach the floor of the den before the lions seized them and shattered all their bones.
verses.6:26: Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, tribes, and languages dwelling on the whole earth: "May peace be multiplied to you.
verses.6:27: A decree has been established by me that throughout my entire empire and kingdom people should tremble before and fear the God of Daniel; for He Himself is the living God, and eternal through the ages, and His kingdom will not be dissolved, and His authority is forever.
verses.6:28: He Himself is a deliverer and savior, working signs and wonders in heaven and on earth, who delivered Daniel from the den of lions."
verses.6:29: Moreover, Daniel persevered until the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
verses.7:1: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream, and the vision of his head was on his bed; and writing down the dream, he encompassed it in a brief account, and touching on it in summary, he said:
verses.7:2: "I was seeing in my vision by night, and look, the four winds of heaven were fighting upon the great sea.
verses.7:3: And four huge beasts were coming up out of the sea, different from one another.
verses.7:4: The first was like a lioness, and it had the wings of an eagle. I was watching until its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the earth and stood on its feet like a man; and the heart of a man was given to it.
verses.7:5: And look, another beast, like a bear, stood on one side; and three rows were in its mouth and in its teeth, and they were saying to it in this way: 'Rise, eat abundant flesh.'
verses.7:6: After these things I was watching, and look, another like a leopard, and it had wings like a bird, four upon itself; and four heads were on the beast, and authority was given to it.
verses.7:7: After these things I was watching in the vision of the night, and look, a fourth beast, terrifying and astonishing and exceedingly strong. It had great iron teeth, eating and shattering, and trampling the remainder with its feet; moreover, it was unlike the other beasts that I had seen before it, and it had ten horns.
verses.7:8: I was observing the horns, and look, another little horn sprang up from the middle of them, and three of the first horns were plucked out from before its face; and look, eyes like the eyes of a man were in this horn, and a mouth speaking enormous things.
verses.7:9: I was watching until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days sat down. His garment was shining white like snow, and the hair of His head was like pure wool; His throne was flames of fire, its wheels were kindled fire.
verses.7:10: A fiery and rushing river was flowing out from before His face. Thousands of thousands were ministering to Him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand were standing before Him; the court sat, and the books were opened.
verses.7:11: I was watching because of the sound of the grand words which that horn was speaking, and I saw that the beast was killed, and its body perished and was handed over to be burned with fire;
verses.7:12: and that the authority of the other beasts was also taken away, and periods of life were appointed for them until a time and a time.
verses.7:13: Therefore I was watching in the vision of the night, and look, with the clouds of heaven one like a Son of Man was coming, and He came all the way to the Ancient of Days, and they presented Him in His sight.
verses.7:14: And He gave Him authority, and honor, and a kingdom, and all peoples, tribes, and languages will serve Him. His authority is an eternal authority, which will not be taken away, and His kingdom is one that will not be destroyed.
verses.7:15: My spirit shuddered; I, Daniel, was terrified at these things, and the visions of my head troubled me.
verses.7:16: I approached one of those standing by and sought the truth from him concerning all these things. And he told me the interpretation of the words and taught me:
verses.7:17: 'These four great beasts are four kingdoms that will arise from the earth.
verses.7:18: But the saints of the Most High God will receive the kingdom, and they will possess the kingdom forever, and for ages of ages.'
verses.7:19: After this I wanted to learn carefully about the fourth beast, which was very different from all of them and exceedingly terrifying; its teeth and claws were iron, and it was eating and shattering, and trampling the remainder with its feet;
verses.7:20: and about the ten horns that it had on its head, and about the other one that had sprung up, before which three horns had fallen; and about that horn which had eyes and a mouth speaking grand things, and was greater than the rest.
verses.7:21: I was watching, and look, that horn was making war against the saints and prevailing over them,
verses.7:22: until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the saints of the Exalted One, and the time arrived, and the saints took possession of the kingdom.
verses.7:23: And he spoke in this way: 'The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on earth, which will be greater than all kingdoms, and it will devour the whole earth, and trample it, and shatter it.
verses.7:24: Moreover, the ten horns of that kingdom will be ten kings; and another will arise after them, and he himself will be more powerful than the former ones, and he will humble three kings.
verses.7:25: And he will speak words against the Exalted One, and he will crush the saints of the Most High; and he will think that he can change times and laws, and they will be handed over into his hand until a time, and times, and half a time.
verses.7:26: And the court will sit, so that power may be taken away, and be crushed, and perish to the end.
verses.7:27: And let the kingdom, and the authority, and the greatness of the kingdom that is beneath the whole heaven, be given to the people of the saints of the Most High, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all kings will serve Him and obey.'
verses.7:28: Up to this point is the end of the word. I, Daniel, was greatly troubled by my thoughts, and my face was changed in me; yet I kept the word in my heart."
verses.8:1: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me. I, Daniel, after what I had seen at the beginning,
verses.8:2: saw in my vision, while I was in the fortress of Susa, which is in the region of Elam; and I saw in the vision that I was by the gate of Ulai.
verses.8:3: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, one ram was standing before the marsh, having high horns, and one was higher than the other and growing up. Afterward,
verses.8:4: I saw the ram thrusting with its horns toward the west, and toward the north, and toward the south, and all the beasts could not resist it nor be delivered from its hand; and it acted according to its will and was exalted.
verses.8:5: And I was considering; and look, a buck of the goats was coming from the west over the face of the whole earth, and it was not touching the earth. Now the buck had a prominent horn between its eyes.
verses.8:6: And it came all the way to that horned ram which I had seen standing before the gate, and ran at it in the rush of its strength.
verses.8:7: And when it had approached close to the ram, it became enraged against it and struck the ram, and shattered its two horns, and the ram could not resist it; and when it had thrown it to the ground, it trampled it, and no one was able to deliver the ram from its hand.
verses.8:8: Now the buck of the goats became exceedingly great; and when it had grown, the great horn was broken, and four horns arose beneath it toward the four winds of heaven.
verses.8:9: And out of one of them one small horn came forth, and it became great toward the south, and toward the east, and toward the strength.
verses.8:10: And it was exalted as far as the strength of heaven, and threw down some of the strength and of the stars, and trampled them.
verses.8:11: And even as far as the Prince of the strength it was exalted; and from Him it took away the perpetual sacrifice, and threw down the place of His sanctuary.
verses.8:12: And power was given to it against the perpetual sacrifice because of sins; and truth will be cast down upon the earth, and it will act and prosper.
verses.8:13: Then I heard one of the holy ones speaking, and one holy one said to another, I do not know whom, who was speaking, "How long will the vision be, and the perpetual sacrifice, and the sin of the desolation that has taken place, and the sanctuary and the strength be trampled?"
verses.8:14: And he said to him, "Until evening and morning, two thousand three hundred days; and the sanctuary will be cleansed."
verses.8:15: Now it happened, while I, Daniel, was seeing the vision and seeking understanding, look, there stood in my sight something like the appearance of a man.
verses.8:16: And I heard the voice of a man amid Ulai, and he called out and said, "Gabriel, make this vision understood."
verses.8:17: And he came and stood beside where I was standing; and when he had come, terrified, I fell down upon my face, and he said to me, "Understand, son of man, for at the time of the end the vision will be fulfilled."
verses.8:18: And while he was speaking to me, I collapsed face down to the ground; and he touched me and set me standing in my place,
verses.8:19: and said to me, "I will show you the things that are to come at the end of the curse, for the time has its end.
verses.8:20: The ram that you saw having horns is the king of the Medes and of the Persians.
verses.8:21: Furthermore, the buck of the goats is the king of the Greeks; and the great horn that was between its eyes, he is the first king.
verses.8:22: Now as for the fact that, when it was broken, four arose in its place: four kings will rise up from his nation, but not in his strength.
verses.8:23: And after their reign, when iniquities have increased, a king shameless in face and understanding riddles will rise up;
verses.8:24: and his strength will be reinforced, yet not by his own power; and beyond what can be believed, he will lay waste to all things, and he will prosper and act. And he will kill the mighty and the people of the holy ones
verses.8:25: according to his will, and deceit will be directed in his hand; and he will exalt his heart, and in the abundance of all things he will put very many to death; and he will rise up against the Prince of princes, and without a hand he will be crushed.
verses.8:26: And the vision of evening and morning that has been spoken is true; you, therefore, seal up the vision, because it will be after many days."
verses.8:27: And I, Daniel, grew faint and was sick for days; and when I had risen, I was doing the king's work, and I was astonished at the vision, and there was no one to interpret it.
verses.9:1: In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, who ruled over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
verses.9:2: in year one of his reign, I, Daniel, understood in the books the number of the years about which the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that seventy years of the desolation of Jerusalem would be fulfilled.
verses.9:3: And I set my face toward the Lord my God to petition and to plead, in fastings, sackcloth, and ashes.
verses.9:4: And I prayed to the Lord my God, and confessed, and said, "I plead, Lord God, great and fearsome, keeping covenant and mercy for those who love You and keep Your commandments:
verses.9:5: we have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have acted wickedly, and we have departed; and we have turned aside from Your commandments and judgments.
verses.9:6: We have not obeyed Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, our princes, our fathers, and all the people of the land.
verses.9:7: To You, Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us shame of face, as it is today to the man of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, to those who are near and to those who are far away in all the lands to which You drove them out because of their iniquities in which they sinned against You.
verses.9:8: Lord, to us belongs shame of face, to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, who have sinned.
verses.9:9: But to You, the Lord our God, belong mercy and pardon, because we have departed from You,
verses.9:10: and we have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, so as to walk in His law, which He set before us through His servants the prophets.
verses.9:11: And all Israel have transgressed Your law and have turned aside so as not to listen to Your voice; and the curse and the execration that is written in the book of Moses, the servant of God, has dripped upon us, because we have sinned against Him.
verses.9:12: And He has established His words, which He spoke against us and against our princes who judged us, so as to bring upon us a great evil, such as has never been under all heaven, according to what has been done in Jerusalem.
verses.9:13: Just as it is written in the law of Moses, all this evil has come upon us; and we have not petitioned Your face, Lord our God, so as to turn back from our iniquities and to reflect upon Your truth.
verses.9:14: And the Lord kept watch over the evil and brought it upon us. Righteous is the Lord our God in all His works that He has done, for we have not listened to His voice.
verses.9:15: And now, Lord our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand and made a name for Yourself as on this day: we have sinned, we have committed iniquity.
verses.9:16: Lord, according to all Your righteousness, let Your anger and Your fury be turned away, I plead, from Your city Jerusalem and Your holy mountain. For because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people are a reproach to all around us.
verses.9:17: Now therefore hear, our God, the prayer of Your servant and his petitions, and show Your face upon Your sanctuary, which is deserted, for Your own sake.
verses.9:18: Incline Your ear, my God, and hear; open Your eyes and see our desolation, and the city upon which Your name has been called; for not in our righteous deeds do we lay down petitions before Your face, but in Your many compassions.
verses.9:19: Hear, Lord; be appeased, Lord; pay attention and act; do not delay, for Your own sake, my God, because Your name has been called upon the city and upon Your people."
verses.9:20: And while I was still speaking, and praying, and confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, and laying down my petitions in the sight of my God for the holy mountain of my God,
verses.9:21: while I was still speaking in prayer, look, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision from the beginning, flying swiftly, touched me at the time of the evening sacrifice.
verses.9:22: And he taught me, and spoke to me, and said, "Daniel, now I have come forth so that I might teach you and you might understand.
verses.9:23: From the outset of your petitions a word went forth, and I have come to make it known to you, because you are a man of desires; you, therefore, consider the word and understand the vision.
verses.9:24: Seventy weeks have been shortened upon your people and upon your holy city, so that transgression may be finished, and sin may receive an end, and iniquity may be blotted out, and everlasting righteousness may be brought in, and vision and prophecy may be fulfilled, and the Holy One of holies may be anointed.
verses.9:25: Know, therefore, and consider: from the going forth of the word that Jerusalem be built again until Christ the leader, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks; and the square and the walls will be built again in distress of times.
verses.9:26: And after sixty-two weeks, Christ will be put to death, and the people who will deny Him will not be His. And a people with a leader who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary; and its end will be devastation, and after the end of the war, decreed desolation.
verses.9:27: And he will confirm a covenant for many for one week; and in the half of the week victim and sacrifice will cease; and there will be in the temple the abomination of desolation; and until the consummation and the end, the desolation will continue."
verses.10:1: In the third year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, a word was revealed to Daniel, surnamed Belteshazzar, both a true word and great strength; and he understood the message, for understanding is needed in a vision.
verses.10:2: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for the days of three weeks.
verses.10:3: I did not eat desirable bread, and meat and wine did not enter my mouth, nor indeed was I anointed with ointment, until the days of the three weeks were completed.
verses.10:4: Now on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was beside the great river, which is the Tigris.
verses.10:5: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, one man clothed in linen, and his waist was belted with refined gold.
verses.10:6: And his body was like chrysolite, and his face like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes like a burning torch; and his arms, and what is below down to the feet, were like the appearance of glowing bronze; and the sound of his words was like the sound of a multitude.
verses.10:7: Now I, Daniel, alone saw the vision; however, the men who were with me did not see it, but an overwhelming terror rushed upon them, and they fled into hiding.
verses.10:8: So I, left alone, saw this great vision, and no strength remained in me; and even my appearance was altered within me, and I withered away, nor did I have any vigor at all.
verses.10:9: And I heard the sound of his words; and as I heard them, I lay stunned on my face, and my face clung to the ground.
verses.10:10: And look, a hand touched me and raised me up onto my knees and onto the joints of my hands.
verses.10:11: And he said to me, "Daniel, man of desires, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand in your place, for now I have been sent to you." And when he had spoken this message to me, I stood trembling.
verses.10:12: And he said to me, "Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day on which you set your heart to understand, so as to afflict yourself in the sight of your God, your words were heard; and I have come because of your words.
verses.10:13: Now the prince of the kingdom of the Persians withstood me for twenty-one days; and look, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to my aid, and I remained there beside the king of the Persians.
verses.10:14: Now I have come to teach you what is to come to your people in the last days, because the vision is still for days."
verses.10:15: And while he was speaking to me with words of this kind, I cast my face down to the ground and kept silent.
verses.10:16: And look, one like the likeness of a son of man touched my lips; and opening my mouth, I spoke and said to him who was standing facing me, "My lord, at the vision of you my joints have been loosened, and no vigor has remained in me.
verses.10:17: And how will the servant of my lord be able to speak with my lord? For no vigor has remained in me, and even my breath is cut off."
verses.10:18: Therefore one like the appearance of a man touched me again and strengthened me.
verses.10:19: And he said, "Do not be afraid, man of desires; peace to you; be strengthened and be strong." And while he was speaking with me, I regained strength and said, "Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me."
verses.10:20: And he said, "Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight against the prince of the Persians. When I was going out, the prince of the Greeks appeared, coming.
verses.10:21: Nevertheless, I will declare to you what is set down in the writing of truth; and no one is my helper in all these things except Michael your prince."
verses.11:1: "Now I, from the first year of Darius the Mede, was standing so that he might be strengthened and fortified.
verses.11:2: And now I will declare the truth to you. Look, three more kings will stand in Persia, and the fourth will be enriched with exceedingly great wealth above all; and when he has grown strong through his riches, he will stir up all against the kingdom of Greece.
verses.11:3: Then a mighty king will rise, and he will rule with great power, and he will do what pleases him.
verses.11:4: And when he has stood, his kingdom will be shattered and divided toward the four winds of heaven, yet not to his descendants, nor according to his power with which he ruled; for his kingdom will be torn apart even for outsiders, apart from these.
verses.11:5: And the king of the south will be strengthened; and one of his princes will prevail over him, and he will rule with authority, for great will be his dominion.
verses.11:6: And after the end of years they will make an alliance; and the daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make friendship, and she will not retain the strength of the arm, nor will her offspring stand; and she herself will be handed over, and her young men who brought her, and those who were strengthening her in the times.
verses.11:7: And a planting from the sprout of her roots will stand; and he will come with an army and enter the province of the king of the north, and he will mistreat them and prevail.
verses.11:8: Moreover, he will lead captive into Egypt their gods as well, and carved images, and also precious vessels of silver and gold; he himself will prevail against the king of the north.
verses.11:9: And the king of the south will enter into the kingdom, and he will return to his own land.
verses.11:10: Now his sons will be provoked, and they will gather a multitude of very many armies; and he will come hastening and overflowing, and he will return, and be stirred up, and clash with his strength.
verses.11:11: And the king of the south, provoked, will go out and fight against the king of the north; and he will prepare an exceedingly great multitude, and the multitude will be given into his hand.
verses.11:12: And he will capture the multitude, and his heart will be lifted up, and he will cast down many thousands, yet he will not prevail.
verses.11:13: For the king of the north will turn back and prepare a multitude much greater than before; and at the end of the times and years he will come hastening with a great army and exceedingly great wealth.
verses.11:14: And in those times many will rise up against the king of the south; the sons of the transgressors of your people will also exalt themselves in order to fulfill the vision, and they will fall.
verses.11:15: And the king of the north comes, and he will heap up a rampart and capture the most fortified cities; and the arms of the south will not hold out, and his chosen ones will rise up to resist, and there will be no strength.
verses.11:16: And he who comes against him will do according to his pleasure, and there will be no one who stands before his face; and he will stand in the renowned land, and it will be consumed in his hand.
verses.11:17: And he will set his face to come to hold his entire kingdom, and he will do upright things with him; and he will give him a daughter of women in order to overthrow it, yet she will not stand, nor will she be his.
verses.11:18: And he will turn his face toward the islands and capture many; and he will make the prince of his reproach cease, and his reproach will be turned back upon him.
verses.11:19: And he will turn his face toward the dominion of his own land, and he will stumble and fall, and will not be found.
verses.11:20: And in his place will stand one most vile and unworthy of royal splendor; and in a few days he will be shattered, not in fury, nor in battle.
verses.11:21: And in his place will stand a despised one, and royal honor will not be bestowed on him; and he will come secretly and obtain the kingdom through deceit.
verses.11:22: And the arms of the one fighting will be overcome before his face and will be shattered, and moreover the leader of the covenant as well.
verses.11:23: And after friendships, he will practice deceit with him; and he will go up and prevail with a small people.
verses.11:24: And he will enter abundant and fertile cities, and he will do things that his fathers and the fathers of his fathers did not do; he will scatter plunder, and spoil, and their riches, and against the strongest cities he will devise plans, and this until a time.
verses.11:25: And his strength and his heart will be stirred up against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south will be provoked to war with many and exceedingly strong auxiliary forces, yet they will not stand, because they will devise plots against him.
verses.11:26: And those who eat bread with him will crush him, and his army will be overwhelmed, and very many will fall killed.
verses.11:27: The heart of the two kings will also be to do evil, and at one table they will speak falsehood; yet they will not succeed, because the end is still for another time.
verses.11:28: And he will return to his own land with much wealth, and his heart will be against the holy covenant; and he will act, and return to his own land.
verses.11:29: At the appointed time he will return and come toward the south; and the last will not be like the former.
verses.11:30: And triremes and the Romans will come against him, and he will be struck, and he will return and become indignant against the covenant of the sanctuary, and will act; and he will return and plot against those who have abandoned the covenant of the sanctuary.
verses.11:31: And arms from him will stand, and they will defile the sanctuary of strength, and take away the continual sacrifice; and they will place the abomination for desolation.
verses.11:32: And the wicked against the covenant will pretend deceitfully; but the people who know their God will prevail and act.
verses.11:33: And the learned among the people will teach very many; and they will fall by the sword, and by flame, and by captivity, and by plunder for days.
verses.11:34: And when they have fallen, they will be lifted up with a little help; and very many will join themselves to them deceitfully.
verses.11:35: And some of the educated will fall, so that they may be refined, and chosen, and made white until the predetermined time, because there will still be another time.
verses.11:36: And the king will do according to his will, and he will exalt himself and magnify himself against every god, and against the God of gods he will speak great things; and he will prosper until the wrath is completed, for the decree has indeed been accomplished.
verses.11:37: And he will not regard the God of his fathers; and he will be given to the desires of women, nor will he care for any of the gods, because he will rise up against all things.
verses.11:38: However, he will revere the god Maozim in his place; and a god whom his fathers did not know he will worship with gold, and silver, and precious stone, and precious things.
verses.11:39: And he will act to fortify Maozim with a foreign god whom he has acknowledged; and he will multiply glory, and he will give them authority over many, and he will divide the land for nothing.
verses.11:40: And at the predetermined time the king of the south will do battle against him, and the king of the north will come against him like a storm with chariots, and with horsemen, and with a great fleet; and he will enter the lands, and crush them, and pass through.
verses.11:41: And he will enter into the glorious land, and many will fall; however, these alone will be saved from his hand: Edom, and Moab, and the chief part of the sons of Ammon.
verses.11:42: And he will stretch out his hand against the lands, and the land of Egypt will not escape.
verses.11:43: And he will rule over the treasures of gold and silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt; he will also pass through Libya and Ethiopia.
verses.11:44: And a report will trouble him from the east and from the north; and he will come with a great multitude in order to crush and kill very many.
verses.11:45: And he will pitch his tent at Apadno between the seas, upon the renowned and holy mountain; and he will come even to its summit, and no one will help him."
verses.12:1: "At that time, however, Michael the great prince, who stands for the sons of your people, will rise up; and a time will come such as has not been from the time when nations began to exist until that time. And at that time your people will be saved, everyone who is found written in the book.
verses.12:2: And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awaken, some to eternal life, and others to disgrace, so that they may always see.
verses.12:3: But those who are learned will shine like the radiance of the expanse, and those who instruct many toward righteousness, like stars for perpetual eternities.
verses.12:4: But you, Daniel, close up the words and seal the book until the appointed time; very many will pass through, and knowledge will be manifold."
verses.12:5: And I, Daniel, saw, and look, as it were, two others were standing: one on this side upon the bank of the river, and another on that side on the other bank of the river.
verses.12:6: And I said to the man who was clothed in linen, who was standing above the waters of the river, "How long until the end of these wonders?"
verses.12:7: And I heard the man who was clothed in linen, who was standing above the waters of the river, when he had raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and had sworn by Him who lives forever: "For a time, and times, and half a time. And when the scattering of the hand of the holy people has been completed, all these things will be completed."
verses.12:8: And I heard, and I did not understand. And I said, "My lord, what will be after these things?"
verses.12:9: And he said, "Go, Daniel, because the words are closed up and sealed until the predetermined time.
verses.12:10: Many will be chosen, and whitened, and tested like fire; and the wicked will act wickedly, nor will any of the wicked understand; the learned, however, will understand.
verses.12:11: And from the time when the continual sacrifice has been taken away and the abomination has been set up for desolation, there will be one thousand two hundred ninety days.
verses.12:12: Blessed is the one who waits and reaches one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
verses.12:13: But you, go until the predetermined time; and you will rest, and you will stand in your lot at the end of the days."

notes.1:3: Latin tyrannorum (literally 'of rulers' or 'of lords/tyrants') renders Hebrew partemim ('nobles'), using Late Latin tyrannus in its older sense of a governing prince or lord.
notes.1:7: The Vulgate renders Daniel's Babylonian name as Baltassar (identical in spelling to the form it later uses for King Belshazzar), here standardized to Belteshazzar.
notes.1:8: The Vulgate reads de mensa regis ('from the king's table') where the Hebrew specifies patbag hammelek ('the king's royal delicacies/food').
notes.1:11: The Vulgate treats the Hebrew title hammelsar ('the steward' or 'overseer') as the personal name Malasar (also in 1:16).
notes.1:20: Latin invenit in eis decuplum super ('he found in them tenfold above') reflects a distinctive Vulgate phrasing without the Hebrew comparative 'better', while ariolos et magos literally denotes 'diviners and magicians'.
notes.2:4: Latin syriace ("in Syriac") renders the Aramaic term for the Aramaic language.
notes.2:5: Latin Sermo recessit a me ("The matter has slipped from me") and domus vestræ publicabuntur ("your houses will be confiscated" to the public treasury) are distinctive Vulgate renderings of the Aramaic.
notes.2:17: Latin spellings Ananiæ, Misaëli, and Azariæ are rendered with standard modern English Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
notes.2:18: Latin alternates between sacramentum ("secret," vv. 18, 30, 47) and mysterium ("mystery," vv. 19, 27-29, 47).
notes.2:20: Latin reads nomen Domini ("the name of the Lord") where the Aramaic reads "the name of God."
notes.2:26: Latin spelling Baltassar is rendered with standard modern English Belteshazzar.
notes.2:27: Latin aruspices (Roman entrail-inspecting diviners) is rendered "diviners."
notes.2:35: Latin favillam literally means "fine ash/dust" rather than "chaff."
notes.2:39: Latin explicitly adds argenteum ("of silver") to describe the second kingdom.
notes.2:41: Latin de plantario ferri ("from the rootstock/seedling of iron") differs from Aramaic "firmness of iron."
notes.2:42: Latin contritum literally means "crushed" or "broken," rendered "brittle" in contrast with solidum ("solid").
notes.2:49: Latin spellings Sidrach, Misach, and Abdenago are rendered with standard modern English Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
notes.3:5: Latin 'symphoniæ' retains the Greek loanword 'symphonia', which Jerome in his Commentary on Daniel understood as a harmonious musical ensemble rather than a single instrument, though modern scholars often identify the underlying Aramaic term as a bagpipe.
notes.3:17: Unlike the Aramaic Masoretic Text, which begins conditionally, the Vulgate follows the Greek Theodotion reading with a direct affirmation: 'Ecce enim' ('For look').
notes.3:20: Following the Greek Theodotion text, the Vulgate specifies 'ligatis pedibus' ('to bind the feet'), whereas the Aramaic text states only that the men were to be bound.
notes.3:24: Verses 3:24-90 preserve the deuterocanonical Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three Young Men, translated in the Vulgate from the Greek Theodotion text and absent from the Aramaic Masoretic Text.
notes.3:40: The Vulgate reads 'ut placeat tibi' ('that it may please You') where the Greek has 'to follow You wholly'; likewise in 3:44, 'in omni potentia tua' ('by all Your power') refers to God's power rather than the enemies being stripped of their own power.
notes.3:65: The Vulgate reads 'omnes spiritus Dei' ('all spirits of God'), whereas the Greek Theodotion text has simply 'all winds' (or 'all spirits') without 'of God.'
notes.3:88: Latin 'infernus' translates Greek 'Hades' (Hebrew 'Sheol'), denoting the underworld or realm of the dead, as reflected in the parallel phrase 'from the hand of death.'
notes.3:92: Following the Greek Theodotion text, the Vulgate reads the singular 'filio Dei' ('a son of God', also renderable 'the Son of God'), whereas the Aramaic Masoretic Text has the plural 'bar elahin' ('a son of the gods').
notes.3:94: Latin 'sarabala' transliterates the Aramaic/Greek loanword for wide Persian trousers (translated 'braccis' in 3:21). In 3:95, 'verbum regis immutaverunt' ('altered the king's word') literally preserves the idiom for disobeying or overturning a royal command.
notes.4:15: Latin germen radicum ejus literally means "the shoot of its roots" (similarly in 4:23 and 4:26), where the Aramaic text refers to the stump of the tree's roots.
notes.4:16: Latin septem tempora mutentur super eum literally means "let seven times change over him" (also in 4:23, 4:25, and 4:32), reflecting the Aramaic verb's dual sense of passing and alternating.
notes.4:18: The Vulgate spells both Daniel's Babylonian name (Belteshazzar, here and in 4:19, 5:12) and the king's name in chapter 5 (Belshazzar) identically as Baltassar, following the Greek Baltasar; standard modern English spellings are used to distinguish them.
notes.4:27: Vulgate eleemosynis redime ("redeem with almsgiving") and forsitan ignoscet delictis tuis ("perhaps He will forgive your offenses") reflect the traditional Greek and Latin rendering, where the Aramaic reads "break off your sins by righteousness" and "perhaps there may be a lengthening of your prosperity."
notes.4:37: In this Latin text, 4:37 opens with Nebuchadnezzar's proclamation and praise (corresponding to Vulgate 3:98-100 / English 4:1-3) before concluding with the king's final doxology.
notes.5:1: Vulgate unusquisque secundum suam bibebat aetatem ("each one was drinking according to his age") is a distinctly Vulgate reading, where the Aramaic text states that the king drank wine before the thousand.
notes.5:2: Vulgate jam temulentus ("being already drunk") renders the Aramaic idiom "at the taste of the wine" more explicitly.
notes.5:5: Vulgate articulos manus scribentis literally means "the joints of the hand that was writing," rendering the Aramaic phrase for the palm or back of the hand.
notes.5:17: In this Latin text, the verse concludes with the inscription sentence (usually 5:25), which gives three words in the Vulgate—Mane, Thecel, Phares (standardized here as Mene, Tekel, Peres)—rather than the four-word Masoretic sequence (Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin).
notes.6:1: In the Vulgate, chapter 6 begins here with Darius's accession (numbered 5:31 in the Masoretic Text), shifting subsequent verse numbers in the chapter by one.
notes.6:4: Vulgate 'spiritus Dei amplior' explicitly adds 'of God,' whereas the Aramaic Masoretic Text reads simply 'an extraordinary spirit.'
notes.6:7: Vulgate 'surripuerunt regi' ('approached the king stealthily') portrays the officials creeping in craftily upon Darius, where the Aramaic verb denotes coming together in a throng or conspiracy.
notes.6:19: Vulgate 'cibi' ('food') renders the obscure Aramaic term often translated 'diversions' or 'entertainment,' and 'dormivit incoenatus' literally says the king went to sleep without supper before sleep departed from him.
notes.6:29: Vulgate 'perseveravit usque ad' ('persevered until') differs from the Aramaic, which states that Daniel 'prospered during' the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
notes.7:4: Vulgate 'leaena' distinctly reads 'lioness' (feminine, matching Latin 'bestia'), whereas the Aramaic has 'lion.'
notes.7:5: Vulgate 'tres ordines ... in ore ejus, et in dentibus ejus' ('three rows in its mouth and in its teeth') differs distinctly from the Aramaic 'three ribs in its mouth between its teeth.'
notes.7:10: Vulgate 'decies millies centena millia' literally states 'ten thousand times a hundred thousand' (one billion), whereas the Aramaic reads 'ten thousand times ten thousand' (one hundred million).
notes.7:14: Vulgate 'Et dedit ei' uses an active verb ('And He gave Him,' with the Ancient of Days as implied subject), whereas the Aramaic reads passively 'was given.'
notes.7:19: Vulgate 'dentes et ungues ejus ferrei' makes both the fourth beast's teeth and claws iron, omitting the Aramaic detail that its claws were bronze; similarly, 7:17, 7:23, and 7:24 read 'four kingdoms,' 'greater,' and 'more powerful' where the Aramaic reads 'four kings' and 'different.'
